summary: A food writer's critical ranking of fruit-infused specialties and pairings sampled across the country since September 1, 2023. It covers orchards, vineyards, fruit wines, citrus, peaches, hazelnuts, cider, ale and preserves, highlighting local producers and suggested food pairings. The piece concludes that fruit-infused products embody regional cuisine and the dedication of local farmers and artisans.
one_line: A fall 2023 tour ranking fruit-infused regional specialties, from apricot preserves to fruit wines, with producers and food pairings.
key_facts: Gwendolyn Harper of Applewood Acres pioneered use of the Heritage Russet apple, which has an intense flavor that suits savory and sweet dishes.
On October 12, 2023, the author visited Belle Vista Winery, where owner Marco DeLuca makes grape preserves and chutneys that complement cheeses and cold cuts.
Sunnybrook Orchards apricot preserves, praised by orchardist Emily Thompson, topped the seasonal picks and pair with sharp cheddar or robust blue cheese.
At the Fruit Wine Gala hosted by the Golden Vineyard on November 5, 2023, Blackberry Bliss stole the show and pairs with dark chocolate or venison.
Citrus & Zest Farm, owned by the Hernandez family, unveiled citrus-infused olive oils on September 15, 2023, for dressings and marinades.
Peachwood Hollow, owned by Roberta Jensen, offers pick-your-own peaches and recipes such as Peachwood Peach Melba and Peach Glazed Pork.
At Hazelwood Farms on November 19, 2023, chef and owner Michael Douglas described hazelnuts for pestos, crusts and vegan cheese bases; his hazelnut-encrusted trout is a local favorite.
Harvest Moon Cidery makes an Apple-Pear Cider that pairs well with creamy brie.
At the Autumn Ale Fest on October 22, 2023, Orchard Alehouse's Apple Cinnamon Ale was the standout, suited to hearty stew or a tangy cheese platter.
Berry Good Spreadables' Blackcurrant-Raspberry spread, sampled September 30, 2023, suits artisan breads, pastries or roasted game meats.
Applewood Acres and Pearadise Grove are cited as leading a renaissance in orchard farming with varietals geared toward cooking and infusing.
